messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's security segment / SOC2 & compliance Qs. Capturing open items here so we can track.

leah: Thanks Maria. Happy to field SOC2 scope questions. Short answers inline.

kai: Two quick customer asks: 1) can we ship syslog/CEF to customer SIEM? 2) will hosted customers be listed in SOC2 scope or only Dedicated/Private?

leah: 1) Yes for Dedicated and Private we support pushing CEF/syslog to a customer-managed endpoint. For Hosted we offer export to customer S3 / GCS as the primary path and can do syslog for enterprise contracts.

ashok: Technical note: syslog/CEF requires a persistent egress tunnel (VPN or PrivateLink), and we need to size the streaming pipeline. We'll produce a doc with throughput numbers.

devon: 2) SOC2 scope: hosted customers are in-scope for Redwoods controls (we're the service), but customer-specific controls (data separation, their access controls) are out-of-scope for our report. We'll include a scope appendix listing regions and major shared services.

kai: Can you clarify data residency? A customer in EU asked whether audit logs and keys can remain in eu-west-1 only.

ashok: We can pin data to a region for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, audit logs are stored in the customer's selected region by default but some control-plane metadata may be replicated for reliability; we'll document what is replicated and why. If strict residency is required, recommend Dedicated/Private.

leah: KMS question triage: BYOK vs Redwood-managed. Customers want to know whether we support HSM-backed keys and whether Redwood can do rotation on BYOK.

devon: We support HSM-backed keys (via our KMS integrations). BYOK keys can be HSM-backed on the provider side. We do not hold customer plaintext keys. Rotation orchestration is available as an opt-in feature for BYOK: Redwood will call customer KMS rotate APIs per configured cadence while logging each step.

kai: What is the recommended rotation cadence and how do auditors view it?

leah: Recommended: rotate wrapping keys every 90 days, sign/verification keys at least yearly unless policy requires faster. Auditors expect documented procedures, role-based approvals, and immutable logs showing rotation events.

maria: Can we provide a short snippet customers can run to verify audit log delivery to S3? Want to share in pre-sales.

ashok: Example (pseudo):

bash snippet:
aws s3api list-objects --bucket customer-redwood-logs --prefix "redwood/audit/2026-07" --query "Contents[].Key"

maria: Perfect. @product_ops can you pick this up and put into the pre-sales FAQ?

product_ops: Yes I will. Please send bullets by 2026-07-09.

leah: A note on machine-readable evidence for SOC2: auditors like a small reproducible package: mapping table (control -> artifact), signed hashes for logs, timestamps, and a list of personnel who approved access. We'll prepare a template.

kai: Any blockers for the template?

leah: Need engineering to export signed log snapshots and include SCIM/role snapshots. @ashok can you confirm export path and retention?

ashok: I can confirm export endpoints and retention config. Will post a short spec by 2026-07-05.

maria: Action items: 1) SOC2 evidence template (leah) due 2026-07-12. 2) Syslog/SIEM technical note + throughput numbers (ashok) due 2026-07-05. 3) Pre-sales FAQ snippet for residency, retention, BYOK (product_ops) due 2026-07-09. 4) Example S3 audit verification snippet (ashok) delivered to product_ops by 2026-07-03. Reply here if any dates are unrealistic.

sec-bot: Reminder created for ashok (2026-07-05) and leah (2026-07-12).

maria: Thanks everyone  closing this thread, will attach outputs to the all-hands notes and ping if any escalations. :thumbsup:
